about: The form a bill takes in each kind of body: what it is (a bill for an act, or an ordinance), how the body numbers it, and its enacting clause. A state chamber's prefix and numbering period come from the recorded research (the old engine's bill-numbering-styles.generated.ts, decision OCD-LEG-NUM-001); its enacting clause from enacting-clauses.json.

federal.source: Bills are numbered in the order introduced, H.R. in the House and S. in the Senate, starting over with each two-year Congress (Congressional Research Service, 'Introducing a House Bill or Resolution', RS22977; the 119th Congress opened with H.R. 1 and S. 1 in January 2025).
federal.enactingClause: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,
federal.enactingSource: 1 U.S.C. § 101: 'The enacting clause of all Acts of Congress shall be in the following form: "Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled."'

local.source: Most municipal clerks number ordinances by the year and their order of introduction (Baltimore City Council 'Council Bill 25-0001'; International Institute of Municipal Clerks, records-numbering practice). Each place's own style is not in the data yet (SG-GOV-local-bill-numbering).
local.enactingSource: Baltimore City Council bill text ('Section 1. Be it ordained by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore, That ...'), data/english/parts/legislation.json key legislation.local-section-first.be-it-ordained.
